rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 15 mm apart across the front of the robot (y = 0.07 m ahead of the axle), so the line stays under at least one or two sensors even on the tighter bends. The 12 mm footprint is smaller than the 25 mm tape, which gives a clean reading across the line. Sensor x positions run from +0.03 m (left) to -0.03 m (right), so the sign convention holds. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority. Mass 0.8 kg and body width 0.12 m keep inertia low and the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03), about 0.0425 m, leaving some margin. Controller: sensor weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2] match the sign convention (left sensor positive steers left). base_speed 1.5 gives about 3070 PWM, which should reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in under 3 s while leaving room to slow on bends. kp 2.0 gives a strong but not saturating steering response (2 units of signal = 700 PWM differential). kd 0.1 damps oscillation without amplifying noise much. ki 0 avoids integral windup on a course with bends. line_loss 'last_direction' keeps the robot turning the way it was going when the tape is lost. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with a modest rms_error, probably around 0.01 to 0.02 m. The main risk is oscillation at speed or going off track on the sharpest bend. Next iteration I want to see whether the speed is limiting completion time and whether steering_oscillation is high, which would mean kd or kp should change.
